source.title: Start/stop signals emerge in nigrostriatal circuits during sequence learning

confidence_rationale: Biological instantiation of the options-framework primitives (learned start/stop bracketing = initiation/termination of a chunked sequence). Grounds temporal abstraction as a real learned mechanism the brain uses to consolidate practised behaviour; neuroscience, not an RL benchmark.
failure_signatures: Provides mechanistic grounding for chunking/termination but is observational neuroscience -- it grounds the class rather than quantifying a floor->competent delta.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In mice on a self-paced operant sequence task, dorsal-striatal neurons and their nigrostriatal dopaminergic afferents develop activity signalling the initiation and termination of a learned action sequence, emerging over learning -- the neural signature of action chunking.
mapping.ree_translation: Biologically validates the options-framework initiation-set and termination-condition primitives (learned start/stop bracketing); if REE builds temporal abstraction, the brain-faithful form is explicit learned start/stop bracketing of sequences rather than fixed-length macro-actions.
mapping.mapping_caveat: Rodent electrophysiology, not an RL benchmark; grounds the mechanism class and the correct form of termination, not a competence number.
mapping.source_context: Mouse dorsal-striatum / nigrostriatal recordings during operant sequence learning.

confidence_components.notes: Cheap as a design constraint (adopt bracketing idea) even if full skill-discovery is skipped; satisfies brain-like-construction.
